text:
Constraint: under 120 words, summarising for a busy manager.

Word count of A: Roughly... title: "Q1 board pack: regional submissions now due Friday 30 October, close of business" (13). Next paragraph: "The deadline moved up from 4 November because the CFO brought the board meeting forward a week. If this causes a real problem, call Priya today rather than emailing." (~29) → 42. "Each region must submit:" (4) → 46. Three bullets (2+3+3=8) → 54. "Requirements:" (1) → 55. "Use the new template (Finance > Board > 2026-27 > Templates). It adds a separate line for software subscriptions, which the board requested." (~21) → 76. "Explain any variance over $50,000 or 10%, whichever is smaller." (11) → 87. "Paste numbers, not screenshots." (4) → 91. "If you're on leave, nominate a delegate and tell Priya." (10) → 101. "Optional: Marcus will run a walkthrough of the new template Thursday at 2pm in the Level 6 boardroom." (18) → 119. Borderline, roughly 119 or so, probably under 120.

Word count of B: clearly longer, about 200 words. It violates the limit.

B also is written in the voice of "I'm writing to let you know," which is odd for a summary. A is better.

**A**
